card.band: 4h. The spec is deep but compact, so a strong agent can finish it in some trials. Typical agents reach about 95% and stall on N0 bracket pairing and isolate edge cases. A weaker model fails on isolates. The surface is large with a fine score curve, but the approach is well known, so the band is at most 3.

card.reference: We write a Rust implementation (about 1200 lines), verified against the oracle on every case.

It exposes a CLI for class-sequence and character-string input.

Band.why: Seed band 4 exceeds the cap without dated public evidence; well-known algorithm; frontier may average near the reference, so the window is narrow.

Build.why: Roughly 2-4 days to write a 1200-line reference, oracle wiring and scorer.

Fit.why: CPU-only Rust, no network at run time; needs vendored crates for the verifier oracle.

Hor.why: Multi-stage pipeline plus CLI and exact-output conformance; 8h tier fits better than 4h for finishing all stages.

Lic.why: Unicode data terms and unicode-bidi MIT/Apache-2.0 permit shipping; exact Unicode-3.0 SPDX text not verified.

Multi.why: Many buckets: BidiTest by class sequence and level, BidiCharacterTest, random strings, L1 and L2 stages, CLI modes; steady credit per stage.

Nov.why: No public task above 0.15; two internal seed neighbours at 0.35-0.37 unverified for overlap.

Real.why: Published UAX #9 rev 52 and UCD 18.0.0 conformance files confirmed at unicode.org; a real standard with a paper trail.

Ref.why: Reference is planned as a complete ~1200-line Rust implementation verified against an oracle on every case; a permissive public port (unicode-bidi) exists to check against.

Seal.why: Hidden files are public UCD data; sealing depends on keeping any copy out of the image (vendored crate tests) and on regenerated random strings.

Surf.why: Hidden set is thousands of conformance cases plus an unlimited random generator with an oracle, per seed claim; file presence confirmed, counts not verified.

spike_plan.kill_if: Conformance files or their expected outputs are present in a package the image would ship (K11), or the partial baseline already scores above roughly 0.9 on every bucket (K8 risk).
spike_plan.pass_if: Oracle reproduces the conformance files; the partial baseline shows a spread of per-bucket scores (isolates and N0 fail while basic cases pass); outputs are deterministic; no copy of the hidden files is found in a vendored crate.
steps: Download BidiTest-18.0.0.txt and BidiCharacterTest-18.0.0.txt from unicode.org into a scratch directory; count data lines per section and confirm the seed's case counts (770k, 92k).

Fetch the unicode-bidi crate source (crates.io or github.com/servo/unicode-bidi) into a separate scratch directory; check whether it ships tests/ data with BidiTest or BidiCharacterTest. If it does, record a seal failure for any image that vendors the crate.
Build the unicode-bidi crate as an oracle in the throwaway container; run it over a 2000-case sample of BidiTest and 500 BidiCharacterTest lines and confirm it passes its own files (oracle sanity).
Write a deliberately partial baseline (explicit embeddings, weak rules, no N0 brackets, no isolates) and score it per bucket to see the partial-credit curve and where it falls off.
Run the oracle twice over the same random-string seed to confirm determinism of level and visual-order output.
Confirm the Unicode-3.0 licence text on the terms page and record the SPDX mapping.

v1.summary: UAX #9 with BidiTest and BidiCharacterTest is a real, sealable-but-tight implementation task: the UCD 18.0.0 conformance files and UAX #9 rev 52 are confirmed, and a permissive Rust port (unicode-bidi) exists. Main risks are that the public conformance files may be copied into the image and that a frontier agent may already reach about 95%, so the band should be 3 with an 8h tier, not 4h.

v2.note: Source files and UAX #9 rev 52 are confirmed, and the unicode-bidi crate (MIT/Apache-2.0) is a strong oracle. The seed itself says typical agents reach about 95% and only stall on N0 and isolate edge cases. Fraction-of-cases scoring then puts the frontier average well above 0.85 of the reference. The algorithm is about 1200 lines and well known, and the seed's own 4 h estimate confirms a short horizon. It also overlaps the other Unicode-algorithm seeds in this batch.
